items.followUp: Define volume and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: This states what density means.
rubric.description: Defines density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that density is mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: The formula expresses density in terms of mass and volume.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Density = mass ÷ volume
ρ = m/V, where m is mass and V is volume.

items.followUp: A body has a mass of 2 kg and a volume of 0.5 m³. Calculate its density.

rubric.why: The principle relates the weight of a floating body to the weight of the fluid it displaces.
rubric.description: States that a floating body displaces a fluid whose weight equals the body's weight.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for clearly stating the equality of the two weights.

modelAnswer: A floating body displaces a fluid whose weight is equal to the weight of the body.

accept: energy transferred from hot to cold
energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body
rubric.why: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.description: Defines heat.

items.followUp: Derive the first equation of motion using a speed-time graph.

accept: area under the speed time graph
displacement=area under the speed time graph
rubric.why: The displacement in a speed-time graph is represented by the area under the graph.
rubric.description: Relates displacement to the area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the area under the graph as the displacement.

rubric.why: The region under the graph from time 0 to t is a trapezium.
rubric.description: Recognises the graph area as a trapezium and uses its area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the trapezium area or giving its area formula.

rubric.why: This is the displacement obtained from the trapezium area.
rubric.description: Writes the displacement as the area of the trapezium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area expression.

rubric.why: Substituting v = u + at gives the second equation of motion.
rubric.description: Substitutes the first equation of motion and obtains the required result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correctly derived second equation.

modelAnswer: Let the speed increase uniformly from u to v in time t; displacement s is the area under the speed-time graph.
The region under the graph is a trapezium, so s = ½(u + v)t.
Using v = u + at: s = ½(u + u + at)t.
Therefore, s = ut + ½at².

items.followUp: A 0.4 kg body moves in a circle of radius 0.8 m at 4 m s⁻¹. Calculate the centripetal force.

rubric.why: The mass is correctly identified in SI units.
rubric.description: Records the mass in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.5 kg.

rubric.why: The radius must be converted from centimetres to metres.
rubric.description: Converts and records the radius in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for r = 0.50 m.

rubric.why: This is the formula for centripetal force.
rubric.description: Gives the correct centripetal-force formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = mv²/r.

rubric.why: The SI values are correctly substituted into the formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution.

rubric.why: The calculated centripetal force is 9 N.
rubric.description: Gives the final force with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 9 N.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, v = 3 m s⁻¹, r = 50 cm = 0.50 m.
Formula: F = mv²/r.
Substitution: F = (0.5 kg)(3 m s⁻¹)²/(0.50 m).
F = 9 kg m s⁻².
Centripetal force = 9 N.

items.followUp: State the two conditions for equilibrium and explain what each condition prevents.

rubric.why: Zero resultant force is the first condition for equilibrium and prevents linear acceleration.
rubric.description: States and explains the first condition of equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant force is zero and 1 mark for linking it to translational equilibrium or no linear acceleration.

rubric.why: Zero resultant torque is the second condition for equilibrium and prevents angular acceleration.
rubric.description: States and explains the second condition of equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque or moment is zero and 1 mark for linking it to rotational equilibrium or no angular acceleration.

modelAnswer: First condition (translational equilibrium): the resultant force on the body must be zero, so the body has no linear acceleration.
Second condition (rotational equilibrium): the resultant torque about any point must be zero, so the body has no angular acceleration.

items.followUp: A wooden cube of sides 20 cm each is completely submerged in water. Calculate the upthrust acting on it.

rubric.why: The cube's side is converted to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the cube's side length to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the side is 0.10 m.

rubric.why: The submerged volume is the cube's volume.
rubric.description: Calculates the cube's volume in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining V = 0.001 m³.

rubric.why: The upthrust equals the weight of displaced water, given by ρVg.
rubric.description: Uses the buoyancy principle or its formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that upthrust is the weight of displaced water or giving U = ρVg.

rubric.why: The density of water, displaced volume, and gravitational field strength are substituted.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values with appropriate units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution using water density and g.

rubric.why: The upthrust is the weight of the displaced water; small variation depends on the value used for g.
rubric.description: Gives the upthrust with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 10 N using g = 10 m s⁻² or 9.8 N using g = 9.8 m s⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: side = 10 cm = 0.10 m; density of water ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³; g = 10 m s⁻².
Volume of cube: V = (0.10 m)³ = 0.001 m³.
Upthrust = weight of displaced water = ρVg.
Substitution: U = (1000 kg m⁻³)(0.001 m³)(10 m s⁻²).
Upthrust, U = 10 N.
